problem_text:
A logistics company must dispatch a technician to perform maintenance at four critical substations within a regional power grid:
Substation Alpha: Grid reference (16,48)
Substation Beta: Grid reference (145,56)
Substation Gamma: Grid reference (61,36)
Substation Delta: Grid reference (139,114)

The fiber-optic communication links between substations, which dictate viable travel paths, have the following exact lengths in kilometers:
Alpha to Gamma: 46.6 km
Alpha to Delta: 139.6 km
Beta to Gamma: 86.3 km
Beta to Delta: 58.3 km
Gamma to Delta: 110.3 km

Due to a permanent geographical obstruction, a direct link between Substation Alpha and Substation Beta cannot be utilized.
Furthermore, network security protocols mandate that exactly one of the following two critical connections must be incorporated into the service circuit: the link between Substation Beta and Substation Gamma, or the link between Substation Gamma and Substation Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient closed-circuit route, measured in total kilometers traveled, that allows the technician to visit each substation precisely once before returning to the origin point.
